conversation.user: Can hempcrete hold up my roof, and is it recognized by U.S. residential code?
conversation.assistant:
Hemp-lime (hempcrete) cannot support your roof on its own—it is a non-load-bearing bio-aggregate insulation material, meaning you always need a structural framing system (such as timber posts and beams or steel) to carry the weight of the roof and floors, while the hempcrete wraps around that frame to form the insulated walls. 

Regarding U.S. residential building codes, hemp-lime is not yet included as a prescriptive material in the standard International Residential Code (IRC). However, builders routinely use it via the alternative-materials provisions of the code, which typically requires working with an engineer or local building official to submit documentation and sometimes preliminary testing for approval.

What style of framing or structural system are you planning to use for your build?
